marks.gloss_en: ודין הוא: as 'weasel' is whatever is called weasel, so 'mouse' is whatever is called mouse -- I include the half-flesh half-earth mouse
או כלך לדרך זו: the analogy runs equally the other way (as the weasel breeds, so the mouse), so the din does not decide; the baraita turns to the verse
או כלך לדרך זו: as the weasel breeds and multiplies, so the mouse [meant is one that] breeds and multiplies
תלמוד לומר 'בשרץ'
Scripture says 'among the creeping things' [including the half-earth mouse]
אמר ליה: ומאחר דשויתיה לים מקום טומאה, מה לי הכא מה לי הכא -- if the sea mouse imparts impurity, the sea is a place of impurity, and 'upon the earth' cannot distinguish land from sea
Rava: once you have made the sea a place of impurity, what difference to me here or there?
והאי על הארץ מיבעי ליה להוציא ספק טומאה צפה, דאמר רב יצחק בר אבדימי -- the phrase is needed for another law
Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi: 'upon the earth' -- to exclude a doubtful floating impurity
תרתי על הארץ כתיבי -- 'upon the earth' is written twice
והאמר מר: whatever is not alike in mating and gestation does not breed from one another
the Master: whatever is alike in mating and gestation breeds and rears from one another; whatever is not alike does not
אמר רב: נס בתוך נס (= p_rav_nes_betoch_nes)
האי פורענותא הוא? -- is this [a miracle]? it is a calamity
מאי נס בתוך נס -- לפורענות: what is 'a miracle within a miracle'? [a miracle] for calamity
Rav: a miracle within a miracle
Scripture says 'that creeps' -- wherever it creeps
or perhaps 'that creeps' means: whatever breeds imparts impurity, what does not breed does not -- and I exclude the half-flesh half-earth mouse, which does not reproduce

say: 'among the creeping things' includes the half-earth mouse; 'that creeps' -- whatever creeps, even the sea mouse; and 'upon the earth' -- on land it imparts impurity, gone down to the sea it does not
'the tzav after its kind' -- to include the arvad, and likewise the nefilim and the salamander

R' Akiva: 'how great are Your works, O Lord!' You have creatures that grow in the sea and creatures that grow on land; those of the sea, if they came up on land, would die at once, and those of the land, if they went down to the sea, would die at once
you have creatures that grow in fire and creatures that grow in air; each would die at once in the other -- 'how great are Your works, O Lord'
whatever is on land is in the sea, except the weasel
Rav Huna b. Rav Yehoshua: the beavers of Neresh are not of the settled land
Rav Pappa: Neresh is under ban -- its fat, its hide and its tail
Rav: if a Nareshite kisses you, count your teeth; if a man of Nehar Pekod accompanies you, it is for the fine cloak he sees on you; if a Pumbeditan accompanies you, change your lodging
Rav Huna bar Torta: once I went to Va'ad and saw a snake wound about a tzav; after some days an arvad came out from between them
the Holy One said: they brought about a creature I did not create in My world; I too will bring upon them a creature I did not create in My world
the limb and the flesh hanging from an animal impart food impurity in their place
